blocks.html: All courses below let you practice as a doctor or healthcare professional. Excludes nursing and basic technician routes. Most entries are via NEET UG 2027. AYUSH and Physiotherapy need lower NEET ranks than MBBS. All cutoff numbers in this document are Open Category.
Modern Medicine

Typical path: MBBS (5.5 yrs incl. 1 yr internship) → MD / MS (3 yrs) → DM / MCh super-specialty (3 yrs)
Total from 12th to super-specialist: ~11-12 years. Entrance: NEET UG → NEET PG → INI-CET / NEET SS.

body.html: The only path to be called "Doctor" in the allopathic sense in India. Hardest cutoffs of any UG medical course.
Realistic Open-category NEET score for govt seat: 620+ for any govt college, 650+ for top govt colleges. Below 600 essentially shuts out govt MBBS for Open category in most states.
After MBBS, specialisations split into broad branches.

entries.title: MD Pathology — the doctor who signs lab reports

body.html: Path: MBBS → MD Pathology (3 yrs via NEET PG). Total ~8.5 yrs from 12th.

The chief who signs every blood report, biopsy, and histopathology report is an MD Pathologist — fully a medical doctor. Lab assistants and BMLT technicians work under this person but cannot sign reports.

Career model: Run an independent diagnostic lab, partner with hospitals, or work in chains like SRL, Dr Lal Pathlabs, Metropolis, Thyrocare. Strong income, low patient interaction, no emergency shifts — often preferred by women MBBS graduates seeking work-life balance.

entries.title: MD Radiology — scans, X-rays, MRI, CT, USG

body.html: Path: MBBS → MD Radiodiagnosis (3 yrs). Highest-paid MBBS branch in India today.
Reads scans, signs imaging reports. Sub-specialties via DM: Interventional Radiology, Neuroradiology. Tele-radiology lets you read scans for US/UK hospitals from home — high foreign-income option.
Radiographer / X-ray technician is a different (non-doctor) route via B.Sc Radiology — covered separately at the end of this tab.

entries.title: DM Cardiology — heart specialist, reads ECG/Echo

body.html: Path: MBBS → MD General Medicine (3 yrs) → DM Cardiology (3 yrs). Total ~11.5 yrs.
The doctor who interprets ECG, Echo, Stress Test and performs Angiography / Angioplasty. Among the highest-earning specialities in India. Heavy work-life cost — emergencies are constant.
Cardiac care technician / Cath lab tech is a non-doctor route via B.Sc Cardiac Care Technology — listed at end of tab.
Path: MBBS → MD Dermatology, Venereology & Leprosy (3 yrs). Total ~8.5 yrs.

Most competitive NEET PG branch. Cutoff is brutal — only top ~500 NEET PG ranks get a dermatology seat. Why so competitive: predictable hours, no emergencies, lucrative cosmetic practice (Botox, fillers, laser, hair transplant, anti-ageing). One of the most preferred branches by women MBBS doctors.
Path: MBBS → MS General Surgery (3 yrs) → MCh Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery (3 yrs). Total ~11.5 yrs.

Covers reconstructive (burns, trauma, cleft lip/palate, cancer reconstruction) and cosmetic (rhinoplasty, liposuction, breast surgery, facelift). Two distinct career tracks possible — pure cosmetic private practice is very lucrative; reconstructive is largely hospital-based.

Sometimes confused with "cosmetic surgeon" — there is no Indian degree called "Cosmetic Surgeon." Cosmetic procedures are legally done by MCh Plastic Surgeons and (for non-invasive) by MD Dermatologists.
Path: MBBS → MD Forensic Medicine & Toxicology (3 yrs). Total ~8.5 yrs.
Doctor who performs post-mortems, signs death certificates in medico-legal cases, gives court testimony. Career mostly in govt medical colleges as faculty or in govt forensic departments.
M.Sc Forensic Science is a separate non-doctor route covered under the Non-Healing Path tab.
Path: BDS → MDS (3 yrs) in specialities like Orthodontics, Oral Surgery, Endodontics, Prosthodontics.

The only undergraduate dental degree in India. Practice as a dentist; can open private clinic. Saturated in metros; less so in tier-2/3 cities. Govt BDS seats typically need NEET 500-580 (Open category).

blocks.html: Ayurveda & AYUSH

Typical path: BAMS (5.5 yrs incl. 1 yr internship) → MD / MS Ayurveda (3 yrs) → Optional certifications / international practice
Total to PG specialist: ~8.5 yrs. PG entrance: AIAPGET (All India Ayush PG Entrance Test).

meta.label: Karnataka Open Cutoff
meta.value: ~350-500 NEET for govt; lower for private

body.html: Practice as registered Ayurvedic Doctor (uses "Dr." prefix). Recognised by NCISM (National Commission for Indian System of Medicine), Ministry of AYUSH, Govt of India.
Notable Bangalore options:

items: Sri Sri College of Ayurvedic Science & Research Hospital, Kanakapura Road, Bangalore. Affiliated to RGUHS. Part of Art of Living campus. Admission via NEET UG → KEA Ayush counselling. Includes Panchakarma clinical exposure.
Govt Ayurveda Medical College, Mysuru — top govt option in Karnataka.
Taranath Govt Ayurvedic Medical College, Bellary.
SDM College of Ayurveda, Hassan / Udupi — highly regarded private.

entries.title: MS Shalya Tantra — Ayurvedic Surgery (Yes, real surgery)

body.html: Path: BAMS → MS Shalya Tantra (3 yrs). Total ~8.5 yrs.
Shalya Tantra is the surgical branch of Ayurveda — rooted in Sushruta Samhita. MS Shalya Tantra graduates are trained in classical Ayurvedic surgery and a defined list of modern surgical procedures.

Legal scope (as of 2025-26): A 2020 CCIM notification permits PG Ayurveda surgeons (Shalya & Shalakya) to independently perform 58 listed surgical procedures, including general surgical procedures (excision of benign tumours, hernia repair, hydrocele, appendectomy), ENT (mastoidectomy, tonsillectomy), ophthalmic, and proctology procedures. Andhra Pradesh formally allowed these in 2025.

Sub-specialty practice: Ksharasutra (medicated thread) for piles, fistula, fissure — this is a flagship Ayurvedic procedure with strong patient demand. Many MS Shalya graduates run dedicated anorectal clinics.
The Indian Medical Association (IMA) opposes this as "mixopathy". Practical reality: the regulation exists, surgeons are practising under it, but expect ongoing public debate.
Main MD specialisations after BAMS:

items: Kayachikitsa — internal medicine (the broadest branch, like MD General Medicine)
Panchakarma — purification therapies, the most marketable internationally
Prasuti Tantra & Stri Roga — obstetrics & gynaecology
Kaumarabhritya — paediatrics
Dravyaguna — pharmacology of medicinal plants (useful for product line, R&D)
Rasashastra & Bhaishajya Kalpana — Ayurvedic pharmaceutics (useful for own product line)
Swasthavritta — preventive medicine & yoga
Rachana Sharir / Kriya Sharir — anatomy / physiology (mainly for teaching careers)

entries.title: Allopathy prescription rights — the honest position

body.html: Short answer: conditionally yes, in some states. Long answer:

items: Maharashtra allows BAMS doctors to prescribe modern medicine after a CCIM-prescribed pharmacology component during BAMS itself. Maharashtra Medical Council registers them with prescription rights.
Other states like Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand have varying rules — usually allowing emergency use and a list of OTC/scheduled drugs.
A national-level "bridge course" for AYUSH-to-allopathy was proposed but has been opposed by IMA and has not been implemented uniformly.
Many BAMS graduates in practice do prescribe modern medicine — this is widespread but legally grey outside the states above.

body.html: Plan A for serious practice: take BAMS in or settle for practice in Maharashtra for cleanest legal allopathy-prescription rights. Or, get the MS Shalya Tantra route for legal surgery rights.

entries.title: Settling Abroad as BAMS — practical paths

body.html: BAMS is not auto-recognised as a medical degree anywhere outside India. But Ayurveda itself is legally recognised or accommodated in several countries. Practical settlement routes:

USA — Ayurveda is not a licensed medical profession at federal level, but practitioners can register with NAMA (National Ayurvedic Medical Association) as Registered Ayurvedic Practitioner / Doctor. Two well-known training/credentialing institutes:

items: The Ayurvedic Institute founded by Dr Vasant Lad (originally Albuquerque NM, moved to Asheville, North Carolina in 2022). Offers Ayurvedic Studies Programs and Gurukula. Strong reputation. NAMA-recognised.
California College of Ayurveda (Nevada City, CA) — Dr Marc Halpern.

body.html: Path: BAMS in India → additional NAMA-approved coursework in US → NAMA registration → private wellness/Ayurvedic practice. Cannot prescribe pharmaceuticals; can offer consultations, herbs, Panchakarma, lifestyle therapy.
Switzerland — Ayurveda is recognised as Complementary Medicine; treatments are insurance-reimbursable in several cantons through registered Naturopath / Ayurveda Practitioner status.
Germany — practise as Heilpraktiker (state-licensed alternative health practitioner) after a German exam. Many BAMS graduates go this route.
Australia & New Zealand — Ayurveda is unregulated; practitioners register with professional bodies (AAA in Australia, NZAAA in NZ). Growing market.
UAE (Dubai, Sharjah, Abu Dhabi) — DHA/MOH/HAAD licenses recognise BAMS for Ayurveda-only practice in licensed Ayurveda clinics and wellness centres. Significant Indian diaspora demand. Pay is good.
Gulf countries (Oman, Qatar, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia) — limited but present.
Other recognised jurisdictions: Sri Lanka, Nepal, Mauritius, Hungary, parts of Brazil, Cuba — Ayurveda recognised at varying levels.

Most practical 5-year plan for settlement abroad: BAMS in India (2027-2032) → 1 year fellowship/internship at Vasant Lad's institute or California College of Ayurveda → NAMA registration → H1B / O-1 / wellness-centre employment-based route to US, OR Heilpraktiker route to Germany, OR DHA route to UAE. Australia & Switzerland are slower but more lifestyle-friendly destinations.

entries.title: BHMS, BUMS, BSMS, BNYS — other AYUSH degrees

body.html: All 5.5 years, NEET UG entry. Use "Dr." prefix. Lower NEET cutoffs than BAMS.

items: BHMS (Homoeopathy) — lowest demand among AYUSH currently.
BUMS (Unani) — Greco-Arabic system. UP, Karnataka, Maharashtra concentration.
BSMS (Siddha) — Tamil Nadu-centric. Niche outside TN.

BNYS (Naturopathy & Yogic Sciences) — drugless therapies, yoga, hydrotherapy. Karnataka has very strong colleges including SDM Ujire and Govt Yoga & Naturopathy College Mysore. Fits the wellness/clinic/product-line vision well — sometimes paired with BAMS-style practice.

blocks.html: Add-on Therapies & Specialisations

Short certifications and skill-stacks you can layer on top of BAMS/BNYS to build a differentiated clinic, train staff, and develop your own product line. Most are 3-12 month diplomas; many can be added during or after the main degree.

body.html: Vital-points therapy from Ayurveda & Kalaripayattu. Used for pain, paralysis, neuro-musculoskeletal issues. Certifications offered by AVT Kerala, Vaidyagrama, several gurukulas in Kerala. Standalone Marma clinics are commercially viable.

5-treatment detox/cleansing protocol. The most commercially successful Ayurveda export — drives wellness retreats from Kerala to Switzerland. PG Diploma in Panchakarma after BAMS, or MD Panchakarma. Essential if you want to run a clinic or retreat centre.

Yoga as therapeutic intervention for specific conditions. Strong programs at SVYASA Bangalore (Swami Vivekananda Yoga Anusandhana Samsthana — deemed university), Kaivalyadhama Lonavla, Bihar School of Yoga, Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram Chennai. Internationally portable credential.

Western manual-medicine system focused on musculoskeletal manipulation. Sri Sri University (Cuttack/Bhubaneswar campus) offers an M.Sc Osteopathy at PG level — verify current intake directly with the university as program details change.

Also see: Indian Academy of Osteopathy (IAO) Bangalore, NIBNS Bangalore. Osteopathy is a fully licensed medical profession in USA (DO degree, equivalent to MD) and recognised in UK, Australia, NZ, France — strong international portability if you pursue full degrees from those countries.
Recognised as a Healthcare Profession by Govt of India since 2019 (Ministry of AYUSH). Diploma and degree courses available. WHO-recognised globally. Easy add-on to any practice.

Short certifications (weekend to few weeks). Not regulated as medical practice anywhere. Useful as service add-ons in a wellness clinic / retreat. Rakkenho (Japanese energy healing / Reiki-family) — niche but has a small following in India and East Asia. Pranic Healing has organised infrastructure via World Pranic Healing Foundation.
Short certifications (few days to few weeks). Commercially popular add-ons in wellness clinics. Hijama has Middle East market relevance — useful if Gulf/UAE practice is on the cards.

PG Diploma or M.Sc in Clinical Nutrition. Pairs extremely well with Ayurveda — Ayurveda's core strength is diet/lifestyle. Lets you offer a "modern + Ayurveda" diet plan as a paid service. SNDT Mumbai, IGNOU, Christ University Bangalore.

blocks.html: Allied Healthcare (doctor-adjacent, separate routes)
Typical path: 4-4.5 yr UG → 2 yr Masters → practice / international bridging exam

meta.label: Entrance
meta.value: NEET UG (15% AIQ via VCI) + state exams

body.html: Veterinary doctor. VCI-registered. Govt seats available, reasonable Open-category cutoffs. Pet-care + dairy/poultry/livestock public sector growing.
Cannot officially use "Dr." prefix in most states. Strong global demand — Australia, UK, Canada, Gulf recruit Indian physios after bridge exams. Sports medicine and rehab are growth areas.
6 yrs. Doctorate-level pharmacy. Clinical pharmacist role with "Dr." prefix. Strong international scope — US (after FPGEE), Gulf, UK. Considerable American hospital demand for clinical pharmacists.
4.5 yrs. Rehab focus — daily-living function recovery. Strong demand in special-needs schools, hospitals, and abroad (US, UK).
4 yrs. Eye exam, vision correction. Not ophthalmologist. LV Prasad Hyderabad, Sankara Nethralaya Chennai are top training centres.
4 yrs. AIISH Mysuru is the top centre — relevant for Karnataka students. Excellent international placement.

blocks.html: Technician Tracks (not doctor, listed for completeness)

entries.title: B.Sc Medical Lab Tech / Radiography / Cardiac Tech

body.html: 3-4 year B.Sc programs. BMLT (lab tech — runs samples, MD Pathologist signs), B.Sc Radiology / Radio-Imaging Tech (operates X-ray/CT/MRI machines, MD Radiologist signs), B.Sc Cardiac Care Tech (assists in cath lab, runs ECG/Echo, DM Cardiologist interprets), B.Sc Anaesthesia / Operation Theatre Tech.
These are technician careers, not doctor careers. Pay caps lower; harder to set up independent practice.

blocks.html: Open-category, affordable seats only. Private colleges with ₹15-25 L/year fees are out of scope. Total govt MBBS seats in India ~63,680 across 456 colleges (NMC 2025-26 matrix). All cutoff data below is for Open Category only.
Central Government Colleges
Entirely outside state-quota politics. 100% seats via MCC counselling on All India Quota basis. Lowest fees in India.

Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education & Research. Two campuses. Among best teaching hospitals in India.
Fees: ~₹4,500/year. Open-category cutoff: Puducherry around AIR 150-200; Karaikal slightly higher.

entries.title: AFMC Pune — Armed Forces Medical College

body.html: Process: NEET UG → shortlist by AFMC → ToELR (Test of English Language & Logical Reasoning, 30 min) + PAT (Psychological Assessment) + Interview + Medical Exam at AFMC Pune.
Open-category cutoff (Girls): Historically requires AIR within top ~500-1000 to make the girls' shortlist.
Catch: Must remain unmarried during MBBS. On graduation commissioned as Short Service Commission officer in Armed Forces Medical Services.
Apply separately on afmc.nic.in after NEET results, around June-July 2027.

blocks.html: Karnataka MBBS Colleges (KEA Government Seat, General Merit)

68 colleges offered KEA government-quota (GMG) MBBS seats in 2026: 23 government, 2 ESIC and 43 private. These seats are filled through KEA counselling for candidates eligible under Karnataka's state-quota rules. The fee for a government seat is fixed by KEA: ₹64,350 a year at government colleges, ₹1,09,350 at ESIC colleges, and usually ₹1,53,571 or ₹1,56,621 at private colleges (a few private colleges differ; see the table).

How to read the cutoffs: each cutoff is the highest NEET All India Rank that got a General Merit (GM) government seat at that college in that round. If your rank is lower (better) than a college's cutoff, that college was within reach in that round. Example: with rank 10,000, BMCRI (2,655) was out of reach in Round 1, while ESIC Bengaluru (11,745) was within reach. Cutoffs move every year, so treat them as a guide. blocks.html:
How to read it, using four ranks
  • At rank 6,000, which is better than 6,539, you would have got Mysore in Round 1, provided you listed it in your options.
  • At rank 7,500, Round 1 was out of reach. In Round 2 the cutoff moved to 8,022, so you would have got Mysore then.
  • At rank 9,000, you would have had to wait until Round 3 (cutoff 9,461).
  • At rank 10,000, Mysore never reached you in 2026 under GM.
The cutoff gets worse in each round because seats open up again after Round 1. Some students who got Mysore move up to a better college, such as BMCRI, take an all-India seat through MCC, or don't join. KEA then fills those seats by going further down the merit list, so worse ranks get in.

Three cautions
  • A later round can show a better cutoff than the round before it. Kempegowda went 19,771 in R2 and then 19,577 in R3, because the Round 3 list covers only students who took part in that round. The note under the table says this.
  • These numbers are GM only. Students in reserved categories (SC, ST, 2A and others) can get the same college at worse ranks, and that isn't shown here.
  • These are 2026 numbers. In 2027 the paper difficulty and seat counts will change, so use the table as a rough guide, not a promise. A practical way to use it: list the colleges whose R2 or R3 cutoff is worse than your expected rank, then add a few safer ones below them.
How KEA Admission Works

entries.title: KEA MBBS counselling, step by step

items: Before NEET results: list only the KEA government-seat (GMG) colleges you would accept, in order of your own priorities (safety, hygiene, location, fees). Do not order them by cutoff.

After NEET results: compare your All India Rank with the 2026 cutoffs in the table above. Round 1 shows early chances; Rounds 2 and 3 show later chances. Keep ambitious colleges above realistic backups.

Register and verify documents on KEA's dates, even if registration opens before NEET results. Medical and dental options can be added only after you download the document verification slip. Then enter, save and submit your college list.
Mock allotment: a practice result only. Correct your list before the editing deadline.

After Round 1, pick one of four choices (KEA: "There will be four choices for UGNEET courses as it is a first round"): Choice 1 = accept the seat and stop; Choice 2 = keep the seat and try for a college higher on your list; Choice 3 = give up the seat and try again; Choice 4 = leave counselling. Pay fees and finish formalities by the deadline. Sources differ on whether Choice 2 needs the full fee upfront; check KEA's notice.

How Choice 2 works: if your list is A → B → C → D and you get C, you can be upgraded only to A or B, never down to D (KEA upgrades to "higher-order options"). If you are upgraded to B, C is released automatically; if not, you keep C.

Giving up a seat: done in person at KEA, Bengaluru, before the stated deadline, and a penalty applies. After Round 2, do not give up an acceptable seat hoping for Round 3: in 2026 penalties started at ₹5,000 and were reported to reach ₹1 lakh later. Round 3 rules change each year.

Holding seats in both MCC (All India) and KEA counselling: if you want the MCC seat, leave KEA by choosing Choice 4 within KEA's window. In 2026 KEA then re-ran Round 2 with the freed seats, using the options already entered; no changes to options were allowed.

National Ayurveda Institutes (AACCC)

AACCC (Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee) fills these seats on All India rank, with no state domicile. It fills all BAMS seats at BHU, ITRA, NIA Jaipur and NIA Panchkula, and half the BAMS seats at AIIA Goa, NEIAH Shillong and NEIAFMR Pasighat, as listed in the AACCC UG information bulletin 2026-27.

Round 2 fills only the seats left after Round 1, so its cutoff can be better than Round 1's (NIA Jaipur went from 31,719 to 29,913). How Admission Works

entries.title: AACCC counselling (national institutes and 15% All India Quota)

items: AACCC fills 15% of seats at government and aided Ayurveda colleges in every state, and the national institute seats in the table above. Seats go by NEET UG 2026 rank.
There are four rounds: Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 and a Stray Vacancy Round (in two phases). Seats left after Round 3 go to the Stray Vacancy Round.

At registration you pick a counselling type. For government, aided and national-institute seats you pay a non-refundable fee of ₹1,000 (₹500 for SC, ST and PwBD) plus a refundable security deposit of ₹20,000. Deemed universities cost ₹5,000 plus ₹50,000.
Each round has a provisional result first, then a final result. Requests about the allotment are accepted only before the final result.
Free exit (leaving without penalty) applies to Round 1 seats. From Round 2 onward, not joining an allotted seat or leaving it forfeits the security deposit.
A seat allotted in Round 3 or the Stray Vacancy Round cannot be left. A candidate who leaves it loses the fees and becomes ineligible for every Ayush UG counselling, central or state, for that year.
AACCC does not set college fees. The bulletin asks candidates to confirm fees, bond and stipend with each college before choosing it.

body.html: Run by Department of Atomic Energy. Heavy research focus. Pipeline to BARC, TIFR, IISc and foreign PhDs.

meta.label: Duration
meta.value: 4 yrs (option to convert to M.Sc, 5 yrs)

body.html: Bangalore-based. India's most prestigious science institute. Accepts NEET score — you can use NEET here even if MBBS doesn't work out. Tiny intake (~120), brutal Open-category cutoff.

blocks.html: Central Universities via CUET UG (Safety Net)

entries.title: CUET UG — Central University Entrance Test

body.html: NTA-conducted. Syllabus is purely Class 12 NCERT — a subset of NEET prep. No reason not to register.
Subject combination for PCMB students: English + Physics + Chemistry + Biology + Mathematics + General Test.

BHU Varanasi — B.Sc (H) various, B.Sc Agriculture
JNU — Integrated Biotech
University of Hyderabad — Integrated M.Sc

body.html: Applications open Feb 2027. Exam mid-May to early-June 2027.

blocks.html: Applied/Professional Tracks (PCMB-friendly)

meta.label: Top Colleges
meta.value: IARI Delhi, TNAU Coimbatore, GBPUAT Pantnagar, UAS Bangalore, UAS Dharwad

body.html: Strong career path: agri-banking (NABARD), ICAR scientist (ARS), agri-business, food tech, AgriTech startups. ICAR colleges give ₹3,000/month stipend. UAS Bangalore is in-city.

B.Sc Biotech (3 yrs) via CUET — DU, BHU, Jamia Hamdard. B.Tech Biotech (4 yrs) via JEE Main / BITSAT — VIT, DTU, Anna University, BITS. Bangalore Bio-Cluster has strong industry — Biocon, Strand Life Sciences, MedGenome.

National Forensic Sciences University (Gandhinagar — Institute of National Importance), Lok Nayak Jaiprakash Narayan National Institute of Criminology & Forensic Science Delhi. B.Sc Forensic Science (3 yrs) → M.Sc → CFSL / state forensic labs / private DNA labs.

DU, Christ University Bangalore, Jain University Bangalore, TISS Mumbai (via CUET). M.Sc Clinical Psychology + M.Phil = licensed Clinical Psychologist under RCI. NIMHANS Bangalore is major PG destination.

entries.title: B.Tech Engineering — only if Maths is strong

body.html: PCMB lets you sit JEE. But preparing JEE + NEET in parallel is brutal and dilutes both. Only sensible if you are strong in Maths. Otherwise drop and don't pretend it's a backup. Bio-leaning B.Tech options: Biotech, Food Tech, Chemical, Biomedical Engineering at NITs, BITS, VIT, SRM.

entries.title: IIT Madras Online B.Sc Data Science

body.html: Can be pursued alongside any other degree. Qualifier exam — no JEE needed. ₹35-40k/year. IIT Madras degree. Strong fallback if you land in a low-prestige main degree; rebuilds your CV.

blocks.html: Govt-of-India Service Routes

body.html: Girls eligible since 2022. UPSC NDA exam twice yearly + SSB interview. Commissioned officer after 3 yrs at NDA + 1 yr at academy. PCMB students can apply for Air Force/Navy streams.
Any decent B.Sc → UPSC at age 21+. IAS/IPS/IFS. Open to all PCMB graduates. Backstop, not a primary plan.
